subject: shotgun
label: shotgun, in the place of the game's models/v_shotgun.mdl, models/p_shotgun.mdl, models/w_shotgun.mdl

measured.lineup: the asset is one of A to D in lineup.png beside models/w_crowbar.mdl, models/w_9mmar.mdl, models/w_sqknest.mdl
measured.lineupTest: asked 4 times, each in another order, which of the four was not made by Valve: judges picked D, D, D, D where the asset was C, B, A, C: passed for one of the game's

M1.reason: The outline is a plain slab with one sloped end: a box of 21.1 x 3.9 x 31.4 with a single diagonal crease (sides.png, FRONT, LEFT, RIGHT, FRONT-LEFT). The brief's pump-action shotgun has a long barrel, receiver, grip, pump and folding stock, and none of that shows in any of the ten views. The silhouette does not read as a shotgun from any side.

M2.reason: Measured length is 31.4 against the brief's 30 (4.8% off), within the 15% band. Width 21.1 and thickness 3.9 are the slab's own dimensions, and the brief gives no width to hold them against.

M3.reason: Parts the brief asks for, checked one by one: barrel, receiver, pistol grip, trigger guard, trigger, pump/forend, magazine tube, folding stock, the hook on the stock's end, front and rear sights. The asset has none of them. It is one solid wedge with no sub-part, no painted marking that stands for a part, and no visible hook (sides.png, lineup.png B vs A, first-person.png left).

M4.reason: The whole body is one flat mid-grey metal (sides.png, first-person.png). The brief asks for black metal with a wooden or dark pump. The metal is clearly off in shade and the pump's wood or dark finish is absent, so the difference is there, not a wrong-coloured part.

M5.reason: The original's markings are absent: no pump grooves or ribs, no screws, no panel lines, no trigger or loading-port detail. The only surface features are a diagonal crease and bevel highlights on the edges (sides.png TOP, BELOW), which are shading from the slab's form, not markings.

M6.reason: Capped and scored from the line-up test, as the rubric directs: the asset is A in lineup.png, and judges picked D (the crowbar) as the one not made by Valve in all four readings, so the asset passed as one of the game's. The pictures themselves do not support that: side by side in first-person.png, it reads as a grey slab, not a shotgun, and a player would not take it for the game's. This is a note on the measure, not a change to the score.

M7.reason: The long axis lies lengthwise as a gun's does, but no front can be told: nothing marks the muzzle end from the stock end, and the front view (sides.png, FRONT) is a low flat wedge. Upright and standing on its origin cannot be confirmed, so the placing is only partly right.

M8.reason: SMAK's check reports no errors. Triangles are 10, well under twice Half-Life's median of 138. The sides and the below view show a closed solid, with no open face, inside-out faces or floating parts a player would see.

W1.reason: In first-person.png the asset sits left and tall, with the hand under its base. The game's own shotgun sits right, held at a grip. The asset has no grip to hold, so it is not held the way the original is. In attack.png (frames 0 to 20) the slab stays near the hand and does not part from it, so the movement holds. The placement and the hold are off.
